title: fine-grained-capability-model-and-siem-slimline-rollout
content:
SUMMARY:
This is a working proposal for moving RBAC v2 from a role-centric surface to a mixed role+capability model, plus a lightweight SIEM export shape ("slimline") that reduces volume while preserving forensic fidelity for enterprise audits. The doc covers: why capability-first for certain product surfaces, the canonical event schema for SIEM ingestion, evidence-sampling heuristics, and a staged rollout plan with safety gates and fallback modes.

Context and motivation:
- Current pain: role explosion + brittle permission mappings in multi-tenant Dedicated/Private deployments. Lots of ad-hoc roles are created for short-lived tasks which bloats audit logs and makes forensics noisy.
- Goals: (1) keep authorization expressive (timebound, contextual, delegable), (2) make audit streams compact and consistent for SIEM and downstream evidence automation, (3) enable a safe incremental rollout with rollback points and minimal customer impact.
- Constraints: must interoperate with existing auth middleware, support offline evaluation for Private installs, and not materially increase latency on request paths.

Design proposal overview:
1) Capability primitives (first-class)
   - Capabilities are fine-grained, composable verbs scoped to resources (e.g., sessions:create, model:invoke:low-priv, admin:billing:read).
   - Capabilities can be granted transiently (timebound), by policy (attribute-anchored), or via delegation tokens.
   - Roles are retained as convenience bundles mapping to sets of capabilities. Migration will expose role->capability mapping as the canonical source of truth.

2) Policy evaluation ordering and fallbacks
   - Local policy cache -> capability allowlist check -> role-derived capabilities -> deny by default.
   - Backwards compatibility: a compatibility shim translates existing role checks to capability checks at runtime. Shim is toggled via feature-flag per-customer.

3) Audit and evidence model (slimline SIEM export)
   - Motivation: full trace of every policy decision is heavy. SIEM teams want consistent fields they can index cheaply.
   - Export event shape (flat, small set of fields). Example event (CSV-friendly):

   timestamp, tenant_id, user_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, capability_set_hash, decision, decision_reason_code, request_id, session_id, geo, client_app, latency_ms, evidence_refs

   - Field explanations (short):
     * capability_set_hash: stable hash of the effective capabilities for the principal at time of request (allows grouping/buckets without listing everything).
     * decision_reason_code: coarse classification (ALLOW_DIRECT, ALLOW_DELEGATION, DENY_MISSING_CAP, DENY_ADMIN_BLOCK, FALLBACK_ROLE_ALLOW, EXCEPTION).
     * evidence_refs: short pointer(s) to richer evidence stored elsewhere (S3 path or internal evidence index id).

   - Full decision traces (expanded events) remain available in long-term evidence store (immutable bundles). SIEM receives slimline events and can request full bundles on-demand for forensic pulls.

4) Evidence automation & sampling
   - Sampling principle: preserve all DENY events and a stratified sample of ALLOW events biased to edge signals (new capability hashes, high-latency, unusual client geos, elevated scope ops like admin:*)
   - Heuristics for sampling: keep 100% of DENY; keep 100% of ALLOW for capability hashes seen < N times in 24h; otherwise retain 1-in-K (K adaptive by volume).
   - ML-driven spike detector: lightweight anomaly detector evaluates recent capability-hash activity; if spike detected, mark related ALLOW events for immediate retention and SIEM alert.
   - Evidence compacting: retained full-trace bundles are deduplicated by request_id prefix and compressed using delta-encoding of repeated KV blobs.

5) SIEM export pipeline (slimline)
   - Export agent (hosted/private): reads slimline events, batches to SIEM in JSON-Lines, supports ECS mapping (Elastic Common Schema) and a "minimal" mapping for customers with storage constraints.
   - Backpressure: when export queue is backpressured, we fall back to local circular buffer + push to S3 for later replay; if buffer full, we drop low-value ALLOW samples only (explicitly not DENY or admin ops).

6) Rollout plan (canary + staged induction)
   - Phase 0 (pilot, 2 weeks): internal rollout to dev/test orgs + 3 selected pilot customers. Enable capability checks behind FF and run in "audit-only" mode (emit slimline events but do not enforce).
   - Phase 1 (soft-enforce, 4 weeks): enable enforcement for non-admin capabilities in pilot tenants. Enable sampling and evidence retention. Collect mismatch metrics between role shim and capability engine.
   - Phase 2 (gradual-enforce, 8 weeks): 10% prod tenants -> 25% -> 50% with automated regressions detection (QA: request error rate, latency, denied-by-mistake rate).
   - Phase 3 (full-enforce): flip default to capability-first; keep shim for 6 months with delete-mode behind enterprise opt-in.

   Safety gates: rollback FF, automatic revert on >1% service error delta or if DENY false-positive rate exceeds 0.5% for two consecutive hours.

7) Migration helper tools and scripts
   - role-to-capability extractor: produce mapping table and suggested reduction (identify unused capabilities).
   - dry-run analyzer: computes predicted denials for a tenant given current mapping (reports top N denied requests and owner teams).
   - reconciliation job: periodically suggests consolidations (merge roles, prune stale transient grants).

8) Observability and dashboards
   - Key metrics to monitor: cap-hash entropy, allow/deny ratio, migration mismatch rate, SIEM export lag, dropped-event rate, evidence-store growth.
   - Dashboards: per-tenant and global. Alert rules: export lag > 10m, dropped-event rate > 0.05%, deny false positive spike.

9) Privacy, retention, and compliance notes
   - Default slimline retention in SIEM: 90 days; long-form evidence bundles retained per customer SLA (default 365 days).
   - PII minimization: slimline event avoids including full user metadata; leverage evidence_refs for detailed PII stored under HSM/KMS access control.

10) Security considerations
   - Evidence bundles signed and checksumed; write-once blobs with immutability flag to prevent tampering.
   - Export agent authenticates to SIEM exporters using per-tenant mTLS certs.

Open questions / TODOs (triage):
- Q1: capability_set_hash algorithm: need deterministic stable hashing that tolerates ordering differences but supports incremental composition. Proposal: canonicalize capability lists (namespace:action:resource) sorted then FNV64. (Action: Miguel to prototype)
- Q2: how to represent delegated capabilities in slimline without leaking the entire delegation chain? Suggest: include delegation_depth and delegation_token_id only. (Action: Priya)
- Q3: retention SLAs for Private installs where customers require 7+ years; need long-term storage plan and cost modeling. (Action: Finance + Legal)

Immediate next steps:
- Prototype hashing and sample exporter (Miguel) — target: internal dev environment by 2026-01-15.
- Add ECS mapping and provide a sample Kibana dashboard (Jordan) — target: 2026-01-29.
- Draft customer-facing migration playbook + FAQ for pilot customers (Samir + Asha) — target: 2026-02-12.

Appendix A: example SIEM event (full JSON-Lines slimline):
{\
  \"timestamp\": \"2026-02-12T15:24:11Z\",\
  \"tenant_id\": \"org_9cX3\",\
  \"user_id\": \"u_77b3\",\
  \"principal_type\": \"service_account\",\
  \"action\": \"model.invoke\",\
  \"resource_type\": \"inference-endpoint\",\
  \"resource_id\": \"ep_prod_42\",\
  \"capability_set_hash\": \"h:0x8a2f33b1\",\
  \"decision\": \"ALLOW\",\
  \"decision_reason_code\": \"ALLOW_DIRECT\",\

  \"evidence_refs\": \"evidence://store/2026/02/12/bundle-req_20260212_ah9\"\
}

Appendix B: rollout playbook checklist (pilot):
- [ ] Create pilot tenant list and feature-flag groups
- [ ] Run role-to-capability extractor and validate mapping with owner teams
- [ ] Enable audit-only mode and baseline mismatch rates
- [ ] Configure SIEM slimline exporter and ECS mapping
- [ ] Validate evidence pull workflow from SIEM to long-term store
- [ ] Run red-team policy fuzz tests against private deployments

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a mid-fidelity working doc; please add inline notes or comments rather than forking the doc. For large design changes, open JIRA ticket JIRA-SEC-2041 and reference this doc id.
- If you have concerns about the sampling heuristics or compliance retention, tag Legal and Compliance early.
